patch.value: Type the browser client against the server routes so public/src carries zero any

The browser client (public/src) was the only untyped part of the pm fleet: the fetch wrapper in api.ts returned Promise<any>, so every call site degraded to any and laundered fields via (data as any).field. This chore derives real response interfaces from the server routes (src/routes/*) and types each call site against them, removing all 112 any occurrences. A new public/src/api-types.ts centralises the response shapes, reusing the domain interfaces in public/src/types.ts. The window.__app bridge, the PWA install prompt (BeforeInstallPromptEvent), and the bulk-update/close DOM-stash pattern (moved to module-scoped WeakMaps) are typed properly too.

grep for ': any|<any>|as any|any[]' in public/src returns zero matches; npm run typecheck (server + 3 frontend tsconfigs) passes; npm run build emits; npm test (160 tests) passes; npm run audit:prod passes; npm run changelog:check passes; no runtime behaviour change except the two WeakMap conversions and the groups member_count field-name fix; response interfaces live in public/src/api-types.ts with TSDoc.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Derived response types by reading every res.json handler in src/routes/pm.ts, projects.ts, github.ts, groups.ts, sharing.ts, auth.ts, admin.ts, extensions.ts. Made api() generic (api<T=unknown>). Added global Window augmentation (AppBridge = typeof __app) plus BeforeInstallPromptEvent on WindowEventMap. Converted items.ts _bulkPayload/_bulkClosePayload DOM stashes to module-scoped WeakMaps. Server mismatch found + fixed: groups list reads g.memberCount but server sends member_count (snake) — badge always showed 0; fixed to g.member_count. Two client endpoints have NO server route: POST /pm/items/:id/history-repair (health.ts) and POST /pm/schema/add-type (config.ts) — both reject at runtime today; typed minimally and called out. sw.ts STATIC_ASSETS extended with /src/api-types.js so the precache test stays green.

patch.value: All 112 any removed from public/src. typecheck (server + frontend sw/scripts), build, 160 tests, and audit:prod all pass. Response interfaces centralised in public/src/api-types.ts with TSDoc referencing each server route. window.__app bridge and BeforeInstallPromptEvent typed via global augmentation. Bulk payloads moved to WeakMaps. groups member_count field-name mismatch fixed; two missing server endpoints (history-repair, schema/add-type) documented.

value.author: claude-code
value.text: Follow-up verification and corrections applied on top of the initial typing pass. First, the UpdateManyResponse interface declared five fields the CLI never emits, namely count, total, updated, items and matched, which preserved fallback chains that could never resolve. Established the authoritative shape by running pm update-many in both modes against 2026.7.28 and enumerating top-level keys rather than reading the express route, which is only a pass-through of result.parsed. Dry-run emits mode, matched_count, dry_run, filters, planned_update_options, item_plans and ids; apply emits the same minus item_plans plus checkpoint, updated_count, skipped_count, failed_count and rows. Narrowed the interface to exactly that, added typed ItemPlan, ItemPlanChange, UpdateManyRow and UpdateManyCheckpoint shapes, and removed the unreachable fallbacks. Second, this exposed a real rendering bug: item_plans entries carry only id and changes with no title, so the bulk preview's title render was always blank. It now renders the planned per-field before and after values, which is strictly more useful and uses data the CLI already sends. Third, went beyond the original scope by eliminating the pre-existing window bridge laundering: origin main carried 15 as-unknown-as casts in public/src, twelve of them ad-hoc window shape assertions in graph and export views. Since the new Window augmentation makes them unnecessary, they were replaced with direct typed window member access, with the two graph globals added to the augmentation, and the resulting trivial single-use window aliases inlined. Count is now 2, both in the service worker where narrowing self to ServiceWorkerGlobalScope and event to SyncEvent is unavoidable because the DOM library ships neither.

value.author: claude-code
value.text: Second follow-up: acted on the CodeRabbit review and, in verifying its findings, found two dead endpoints and fixed them properly. CodeRabbit raised five findings; four were valid and one was not. Valid: the CalendarListItem interface was a field-for-field duplicate of CalendarEvent and is now an alias so the two cannot drift; the priority chip interpolated a raw value so it rendered P-undefined when the CLI omits priority while the dot and label were already guarded; and two client calls target routes the server never mounted. Not valid: the claim that the guide response needed a topic envelope because guide.ts reads data.topic and retains an unsafe cast, since guide.ts contains neither. The two dead endpoints were the important part. The health view rendered Repair and Dry Run controls posting to an item history-repair route, and the config view's add-type control posted to a schema add-type route, and neither route existed anywhere in the server, so both controls failed for every user since they shipped. Rather than hiding the buttons, both routes are now implemented following the established runPm pattern, which means they inherit the router-level write guard that already returns 403 to view-only collaborators. Three things had to be established empirically. The CLI subcommand is the hyphenated schema add-type, not schema add type, which the help text's add slash remove type slash status slash field shorthand does not make obvious. Both actions dispatch in-process through the SDK PmClient rather than spawning, so they needed entries in the runner's positional-key map; without them the positionals were silently dropped and the SDK rejected the call with a missing subcommand error. And the history-repair payload carries no message field at all, so the health toast's data.message fallback always dumped the raw JSON blob; it now summarises the real counts and reports a verification failure distinctly. Added seven integration tests that run a real pm init workspace and assert real effects, including that a registered type is visible to a separate pm process, that a flag-like item id cannot become a bulk repair of every stream, and that a 403 leaves no side effect behind.
